Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Copying a couple folks who will help with the technical and contractual details. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a short evidence packet and a shared dashboard link. Happy to review on a call if you'd like.

1) SLOs we publish: availability SLO = successful request rate (2xx) 99.9% over a rolling 30-day window; latency SLO = p95 end-to-end response time <= 300ms for text-gen single-turn (window: 30-day rolling). We can provide alternative thresholds for high-throughput paths.
2) Measurements: server-side collection at ingress/egress, aggregated per 1-minute buckets; sampling only for full tracing to reduce PII surface (default measurement is deterministic per request).
3) Alerts: two-tier policy — operational alerts to on-call (pager) for sustained SLO breach (>10 minutes) and notification alerts to customer Slack/email for transient violations; we can map recipients per account.
4) Customer access: read-only dashboard links, CSV export for windows, and role-based dashboard invites (SSO integration available). Raw traces are viewable on request under NDA for specific audits.
5) Evidence: we provide exportable CSVs, Grafana snapshots, and a short attestation document.
6) Temporary SLA variance: yes, we support a formal request path for scheduled maintenance or planned capacity bursts. Requests are reviewed, approved with a timebox, and any credits are documented in an addendum.

Stephanie — quick technical writeup below you can paste into procurement. Happy to expand if they ask for raw traces or schema.

1) Exact SLO definitions (publishable wording):
- Availability: "Successful request rate (HTTP 2xx) >= 99.9% measured over a rolling 30-day window, aggregated in 1-minute intervals. Failed requests include 5xx and timeouts; client re-tries are de-duplicated using request IDs for measurement."
- Latency: "p95 end-to-end response latency < 300ms for standard text-generation single-turn requests, measured over a rolling 30-day window. Latency is measured at egress (time when the first token is returned to the client)."

2) Collection & aggregation:
- Server-side instrumentation at ingress/egress using deterministic counters; per-request metadata (request_id, model_variant, region) is recorded.
- Aggregation frequency: 1-minute rollups, retained for 90 days for dashboarding; 13 months for SLA attestation exports.
- Sampling: full request counts for SLO computation; traces and payloads are sampled (configurable) to minimize PII exposure — default 1% for full traces, higher under debugging.

3) Alerting policy:
- Transient breach: system creates a customer notification (email + Slack) for p95 or availability deviation lasting 1 minute; no paging.
- Sustained breach: if a breach persists beyond a configured window (default 10 minutes), on-call is paged (PagerDuty), and a bridge is opened. Customers can opt into paging for faster escalation.

4) Customer access:
- Read-only dashboard link (links use SSO; can be whitelisted per account).
- CSV exports: selectable windows (1h/1d/30d) and raw 1-minute buckets available as CSV.
- Raw traces: available under NDA & audit request; we provide redacted traces by default.

5) Audit evidence:
- We ship a zip with (a) 1-minute bucket CSVs for the requested window, (b) Grafana snapshots, (c) a signed attestation PDF.

6) Temporary SLA variance (proposed):
- Eligibility: documented, customer-initiated request for scheduled maintenance or planned burst > baseline capacity.
- Request process: customer submits request 5 business days prior with start/end times and expected impact; Redwood reviews technical feasibility.
- Approval: engineering & sales sign-off; variance is timeboxed (max 72 hours standard; extensions by exception).
- Credits: if agreed variance results in measurable breach, credit is pro-rated for the timeboxed period per the SLA addendum.

Attached: example-instrumentation-snippets.txt (small code snippets showing SDK counters and sampling).

-Rishi
